candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide care and education for the adolescent client ages 3 through 17 years; educate client about preventive care and health maintenance recommendations
candidate.educational_objective: Support developmentally appropriate private adolescent preventive care while explaining confidentiality and its legal/safety limits.

options.A: Private time is appropriate only for services a minor can consent to independently; routine preventive counseling requires a parent present.
options.B: Private time is developmentally appropriate; we will explain confidentiality and its limits and follow applicable laws and policies here.
options.C: Private time is appropriate, but a complete summary must be given to the parent afterward because confidentiality does not apply here.
options.D: Private discussion can occur only after a parent authorizes it, because parental permission determines confidentiality at preventive visits.

candidate.rationale: Private time is developmentally appropriate in adolescent preventive care. AAP guidance supports confidential adolescent care and time alone while requiring clinicians to explain the limits of confidentiality and follow applicable law and policy. The prior option C was rewritten because it could also be interpreted as correct; the revised distractor now falsely requires routine parental disclosure.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Developmentally appropriate private time and confidential adolescent care are recommended, while clinicians must explain confidentiality limits and follow applicable jurisdictional law/policy.
candidate.source_document_title: American Academy of Pediatrics — Confidentiality in the Care of Adolescents: Policy Statement
